title: Introduction to Foundational Concepts of Electrochemistry

children.text: An electric current consists of moving charge, such as electrons or ions, flowing through a closed circuit due to a difference in electrical potential. This principle is fundamental to many technologies, from powering household appliances to running complex industrial machinery.

Oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions involve the transfer of electrons between substances. Oxidation is the loss of electrons, while reduction is the gain of electrons. Balancing these reactions is crucial for applications like battery operation, where chemical energy is converted to electrical energy, and industrial processes involving electroplating metals.

Understanding electric currents and redox reactions is essential in everyday technologies, such as smartphones' batteries and the electrochemical processes used in metal refining and corrosion prevention.
